problem: Files and projects grow past what an agent can hold; it slows down, loses the thread and starts inventing.
arrow_default: Source files target 300 lines, hard cap 500. A file already over the cap may not grow. Splitting a big file is its own packet with behaviour-preserving checks.
enforced_by: deterministic line count on changed files at verification
onboarding_can_change: company limit (e.g. a max-lines lint rule), exempt paths (generated, migrations, fixtures), ratchet when the repo is already over

problem: Compaction and long sessions drop decisions and fixes; people re-explain; recalled memory is noisy or wrong.
arrow_default: No long-lived agent sessions. Truth lives in the event log and a structured decisions store, written when the decision is made. Every agent starts from a packet, not a chat history.
enforced_by: event log + typed knowledge entries (fact / decision / constraint) looked up by id
onboarding_can_change: import the company's existing decision records (ADRs) as decisions

problem: Agents invent symbols and logic, and write against library versions other than the installed one (the Stack Overflow rows show how often APIs change between versions).
arrow_default: Installed versions beat memory: onboarding records exact versions of the runtime and key libraries; workers read the installed package/type definitions before using an API; typecheck and build are part of every packet's proof.
enforced_by: orchestrator re-runs typecheck/build/tests; version table in the profile
onboarding_can_change: company pins, internal libraries and their docs

problem: Agents claim tests pass, report success on empty output, write tests that test nothing, or leave TODO placeholders.
arrow_default: Done means Arrow re-ran the checks and they passed. A new check must fail on the base code first. Added lines may not contain placeholders (TODO / FIXME / not implemented). Existing tests may not lose assertions.
enforced_by: verify.ts re-run + tamper guard (built); red-first and placeholder scan (to build)
onboarding_can_change: a company TODO format with a ticket id is allowed

problem: Each fix attempt makes it worse; regressions get chased; the same advice repeats; rollback is hard.
arrow_default: One retry with the failure report, one architect re-aim of the packet, then a person. Every attempt is a commit, so rollback is one reset. A fresh worker each time instead of a thrashing chat.
enforced_by: loop manager budgets per failure class (decide.ts, config.ts)
onboarding_can_change: budgets per company or per repo

problem: Agents rewrite working code, remove dependencies, break unrelated behaviour, damage the environment, delete a database during a freeze.
arrow_default: A packet may change only its listed files. Critical rules protect paths. Each worker has its own worktree; nothing is pushed. No production credentials by default; destructive commands are refused; a code freeze stops all workers.
enforced_by: scope + protected-path checks (built); command guard and freeze flag (to build)
onboarding_can_change: the company's protected paths, environments and freeze windows

problem: Generated code ignores the project's naming, structure, typing and error handling, overengineers, and pulls in obscure libraries.
arrow_default: Onboarding turns the repo's conventions into rules. The architect runs the sizing ladder (reuse before build). A new dependency needs approval at the plan check. The repo's lint and format commands join every packet's proof.
enforced_by: onboarder output + plan check + verification commands
onboarding_can_change: this is the category onboarding exists for: the company's rules replace Arrow's defaults

category: Documentation sprawl (from our own run, not the dataset)
problem: Agents and subagents write a markdown file per step until nobody can find anything.
arrow_default: Workers may not add .md files. What an agent learns goes into the event log and the decisions store, not new files.
enforced_by: deterministic check on added files at verification
onboarding_can_change: allowed doc paths the company requires (e.g. docs/adr/**, CHANGELOG.md, README updates)

problem: Parallel agent sessions have no shared view: they duplicate work, contradict each other, fight over files and ports, and leave processes behind.
arrow_default: One shared ledger that only the orchestrator writes, rebuilt every few seconds from what actually runs: live agents, worktrees, which files each packet may change, and which processes hold which local ports. No agent edits it. Each worker is told who runs beside it and gets its own port range. Anything a finished agent left behind (processes, worktrees) is reaped.
enforced_by: ledger.ts (built from the event log + ps/lsof/git worktree), ledger-scan.ts (reaping), per-worker port ranges and a ledger brief in every worker prompt

problem: Code that runs but misses the intent, or behaves differently for the same input.
arrow_default: A project manager writes the spec with acceptance in the person's own terms and asks only what it can't decide, with a real example. The architect cites the design doc in the packet.

problem: Installs, toolchains, platforms, certificates and credentials break before any code is written; setup costs erase the time saved.
arrow_default: Onboarding detects the toolchain (runtime versions, package manager, lockfile) and a plain install command for a fresh worktree (node_modules in the worktree, a venv for Python — no Docker), lists required environment variables by name, and treats a failed install as an environment problem for a person, never as a code failure to retry.
enforced_by: profile commands (built); version and env-var check (to build); failure classes (built)
onboarding_can_change: the company's install command and pinned runtime versions

problem: Review can't keep up; people can't own code they don't understand; subtle mismatches slip through.
arrow_default: Small packets with a budget on diff size; plain-language spec and plan; proof shown before the diff; one branch per task, never pushed.
enforced_by: plan check and packet size (built); diff budget (to build)

category: Trust in what agents are given
problem: Shared skills are unvetted or stale; memory can keep hostile instructions; agents hold keys; AI audits miss real bugs and flag false ones.
arrow_default: No third-party skills by default; prompts are versioned in the repo; untrusted content (issues, web pages) is data, never instructions; workers get only the secrets their packet names; added lines are scanned for secrets; security claims need a person.
enforced_by: prompt contract (built); env allow-list and secret scan (to build)
onboarding_can_change: the company's approved tools and MCP servers

problem: Agents skip or misorder tool calls, pass wrong arguments, don't wait for async work, repeat actions, and fail without a trace.
arrow_default: Code routes, not the model: decide.ts picks every next step; every agent result is validated against a schema; every failure has a class and a bounded path; every step has an idempotent subject; the event log plus transcripts is the trace.
onboarding_can_change: nothing to change — this is how Arrow itself runs

category: Out of scope: business and support automation
problem: Customer-support bots, sales/marketing agents, tone of voice.

category: Out of scope: general programming questions
problem: Language semantics, performance curiosities, app-store policy, git how-to.

category: Out of scope: people and organisations
problem: Skill atrophy, management mandates, study results.
